_doc: A line on each of the city's venues (see venues.json, built by scripts/build_map.py) — what anyone who knows Gotham knows of them. Read by the Codex and by places.note; his own edits in the Codex take precedence.

notes.Bleak House: A Dickens-themed pub in a listed Old Gotham townhouse: candles in bottles, a fire that never goes out, and lawyers from the courthouse pretending they aren't drinking at noon.
notes.Copper Kettle: A dockworkers' bar in Waterloo with copper-topped tables worn green; shift whistles are the only clock anyone trusts in here.
notes.Dock 9: A shipping-container bar on the Port's Park waterfront — cheap beer, a forklift for a doorman, and cargo nobody asks about in the back lot.
notes.Gin Alley: A Narrows gin joint down a passage you'd walk past twice; the bathtub gin is a joke on the menu and possibly not a joke.
notes.Kane's Tap: Burnside's craft-beer bar, eighteen taps and a chalkboard of pours named after Gotham's founding families, none of them flattering.
notes.Last Call: A Bowery dive that opens at four in the afternoon and shuts when the bartender cries. The jukebox has three working songs.
notes.O'Malley's: The Bowery's oldest Irish bar: cops at one end, the people they arrest at the other, and a truce about the dartboard.
notes.Saint Mike's: A Crime Alley bar in a deconsecrated chapel; the confession booth is a snug and the priest-collared barman hears plenty.
notes.Shamrock: A Tricorner shot-and-beer bar where the longshoremen's union still holds meetings, and the meetings still end in fights.
notes.The Corner Pocket: A Crime Alley pool hall with sticky felt and sharper players; half of Gotham's small-time debts get settled over the eight ball here.
notes.The Crooked Mile: Burnley's neighbourhood local, crooked floorboards and all — trivia on Tuesdays, and a regular who's won it since 1998.
notes.The Drowned Man: A Tricorner waterfront bar with a ship's figurehead over the door and a bell rung for every sailor who doesn't come back.
notes.The Hollow: A Narrows basement bar under a boarded-up laundromat; no sign, no windows, and the best whiskey in the worst part of town.
notes.The Iron Stool: An Old Gotham bar built from a foundry's leavings — stools welded to the floor after one too many were thrown.
notes.The Lantern: A Burnley bar strung with a hundred paper lanterns; quiet, warm, and where first dates go to see if there'll be a second.
notes.The Nightjar: A Waterloo cocktail bar that opens at midnight; Blüdhaven's night-shift nurses and cops drink side by side and say nothing.
notes.The Rusty Anchor: A Chinatown sailors' bar from when the docks came this far inland: nets on the ceiling, mahjong in the back, and a parrot that swears in Cantonese.
notes.The Wet Rat: A Robinsville dive whose flooded basement gave it the name and kept the health inspector away for a decade.
notes.Black Cat Café: Avalon Heights' cat café — eleven cats, one of whom has bitten a city councillor and is a local hero for it.
notes.Café Lune: A Halyard Square café with moon-phase pastries and a patio that catches Blüdhaven's one sunny hour.
notes.Common Grounds: Old Gotham's quiet coffee house, chess boards on every table and a no-phones rule the owner enforces with a stare.
notes.Cup of Joe's: A University District coffee counter open twenty-four hours for the thesis crowd; the refills are free and the despair is ambient.
notes.Drip: A Burnside pour-over bar where a cup takes eleven minutes and the baristas have opinions about your choices.
notes.Grindhouse Coffee: Upper West Side espresso in a former grindhouse cinema, horror posters still on the walls and slasher films on Fridays.
notes.Kettle & Crow: A Coventry tea-and-coffee house in a converted rookery, crows on the sign and real ones on the gutters.
notes.Moka: A Cherry Hills café where the old money takes its Sunday brunch and pretends not to see who's sitting with whom.
notes.Perk: A Diamond District grab-and-go for traders, open at five and out of everything by nine.
notes.Pour House: A Burnside coffee shop by day and open-mic bar by night; the poetry is mostly about Gotham and mostly bad.
notes.The Daily Grind: The University District's student café, where every table has a laptop and every laptop has a deadline.
notes.The Roastery: A Fashion District roaster that sources single-origin beans and sells them to models in very small cups.
notes.Third Wave: A Burnside café-bike shop hybrid — oat milk at the front, derailleurs at the back, both priced like art.
notes.Grace Chapel: A small Burnley chapel that runs the soup kitchen on Fridays and asks nobody's name at the door.
notes.Holy Trinity: Coventry's Episcopal church, red-brick and tidy, with a bell tower the kids dare each other to climb.
notes.Our Lady of the Harbor: The Tricorner fishermen's church; the nets are blessed every spring and the dead are remembered on a wall of names.
notes.St. Aidan's: Bristol's parish church, all flint and stained glass — the Waynes' pew is near the front and usually empty.
notes.St. Jude's: An Old Gotham church for lost causes, fittingly; the candle stand by the door never goes dark.
notes.St. Swithin's: A crumbling Old Gotham church whose roof leaks on the altar every time it rains — so, always.
notes.Cineplex 12: An Old Gotham multiplex with sticky floors and twelve screens, three of which have working sound.
notes.Majestic: Blüdhaven's grand old picture palace in Halyard Square, gilt and velvet, running classics to half-empty rows.
notes.Odeon Gotham: The Fashion District's premiere house — red carpets, flashbulbs, and Bruce Wayne leaving early through a side door.
notes.Starlite Drive-In: Burnside's drive-in on the old rail yard, double features under the stars and the bridge lights.
notes.The Bijou: A Kane Heights art-house cinema showing foreign films to people who'd rather you knew they'd seen them.
notes.The Paramount: A Diamond District movie palace restored with Wayne Foundation money; the organ still rises out of the floor before the feature.
notes.The Rex: A New Town cinema with recliners, cocktails and tickets priced to keep New Town new.
notes.Ace of Clubs: A Fashion District casino-club: card tables upstairs, a dance floor below, and a dress code enforced by very large men.
notes.Babylon: A Crime Alley megaclub in a former bank vault — bass you feel in your teeth and a VIP room behind a real safe door.
notes.Catacombs: A Bowery club in the old subway tunnels, candles in skull sconces and a crowd that dresses for the theme every night.
notes.Club Noir: A members-only CBD jazz club, black lacquer and smoke; deals get made in the booths that never make the papers.
notes.Grin: A Diamond District club everyone says the Joker once owned; the owner encourages the rumour and the smile on the sign.
notes.Low Tide: A Fashion District club at water level with glass floors over the river — models, money and the odd fish.
notes.Midnight Mass: A Crime Alley goth club in an old church: organ remixes, black lipstick and a strict no-daylight policy.
notes.Neon Saint: Burnside's queer dance club, pink neon halos and the best Saturday night in the city by a mile.
notes.Sixth Sin: A CBD club themed on the seven deadly sins — the sixth floor is envy, and the bouncers decide who gets in.
notes.Smoke & Mirrors: A Chinatown magic club where the tricks are real and so, some say, is the gambling in the basement.
notes.Static: An Amusement Mile electronic club in a dead arcade, pinball machines for seats and the Ferris wheel lit through the windows.
notes.The Aviary: An Old Gotham rooftop club among the gargoyles — the Penguin's crowd, some nights, and nobody admits it.
notes.The Blue Mask: A Crime Alley masquerade club; everyone's in a mask and nobody's who they say, which suits everyone.
notes.The Gilded Cage: An Old Gotham burlesque club in a birdcage-shaped room, the dancers in swings and the tips in gold.
notes.The Gutter: An Amusement Mile punk dive by the boardwalk, sticker-plastered and loud enough to drown out the roller coaster.
notes.The Laughing Fish: A Burnside comedy club named after the most infamous Joker stunt; the comics do the bit, the city winces.
notes.The Pit: An Amusement Mile fight club behind the arcade, bare knuckles and bets in cash; GCPD knows and gets paid not to.
notes.The Rookery: A Bowery club in a crumbling theatre, rooks painted on the ceiling and the Penguin's people at the bar.
notes.The Stacked Deck: A Diamond District card club for high rollers; the house always wins, and the house is Cobblepot.
notes.Velvet Hour: A Bowery cocktail lounge, red velvet and candlelight — the place to meet someone you shouldn't.
notes.Big Belly Burger: Gotham's favourite burger chain, Burnside branch: the Belly Buster, the shakes, and a queue at 2 a.m. that's half masked vigilantes, rumour says.
notes.Dixon's: A University District diner with a professor-for-a-day board and pancakes the size of the textbooks.
notes.Harbor Grill: An Old Gotham seafood diner where the clam chowder's been on the stove, in one form or another, since 1952.
notes.Jackie's: Burnley's all-day diner, run by Jackie for forty years; she knows your order and your business.
notes.Lucky Seven: A Tricorner diner open seven days and seven nights, lucky for anyone who needs eggs at 4 a.m. after a shift on the docks.
notes.Ma Gunn's: An Upper West Side diner with a reform-school past — Ma Gunn ran a school for young crooks once, and still cuts pie like a threat.
notes.Nite Owl: A Kane Heights night diner with an owl clock whose eyes follow you, and the best grilled cheese after midnight.
notes.Pearl's: A City Hall District lunch counter where aldermen eat meatloaf and make deals over rice pudding.
notes.Rosie's: A Coventry family diner with a rotating pie case and Rosie's grandchildren doing homework in the back booth.
notes.Sal's All-Night: Blüdhaven's Halyard Square diner, open all night every night; Dick has a booth and Sal has stopped asking about the bruises.
notes.The Blue Plate: A Crime Alley diner with a blue-plate special that hasn't changed since the Waynes were alive.
notes.The Midnight Diner: A Chinatown diner that only opens at midnight, cooking whatever you ask for if the chef has the ingredients.
notes.Engine 23: Burnside's firehouse, an old brick station with a dalmatian named Spot and a chili cook-off they always lose.
notes.Engine 41: Old Gotham's busiest firehouse; the old quarter's timber and tenements keep Engine 41 out every night.
notes.Engine 9: New Town's shiny firehouse, glass bay doors and a ladder truck that can reach the forty-second floor.
notes.Ladder 17: Robinsville's ladder company, famous for the night they saved a whole tenement and the mayor forgot to thank them.
notes.Ladder 4: The Upper West Side's ladder company, crews who know every brownstone fire escape by heart.
notes.Crossfire: A New Town CrossFit box where finance bros flip tractor tyres at six in the morning and talk about it all day.
notes.Iron Works Gym: A CBD power gym in an old foundry — chalk dust, iron plates, and a sign that says no mirrors, no excuses.
notes.Knuckle House: A Fashion District boxing studio for people who look good doing it; the owner was a contender once.
notes.Peak Fitness: The Upper East Side's members-only gym: steam rooms, personal trainers and memberships that cost a car.
notes.Southpaw Boxing: A Burnside boxing gym with a free youth programme — Jason's been seen in the back, teaching kids to keep their guard up.
notes.Wildcat Gym: Tricorner's old boxing gym, founded by the heavyweight Ted Grant; still sweat-soaked and still free for kids off the street.
notes.Harbor Inn: A City Hall District hotel by the old harbour, where visiting politicians stay to be seen being frugal.
notes.Hotel Noir: A Diamond District boutique hotel, all black marble and discretion; the night manager keeps secrets for a living.
notes.Hotel Ventura: A Diamond District business hotel with a sky bar on the thirtieth floor and a view of Wayne Tower.
notes.Night & Day Motel: A CBD motel rented by the hour as often as the night; the sign flickers and so do the guests.
notes.The Ashcroft: New Town's glass-tower hotel, rooftop pool and all, where new money comes to prove it.
notes.The Belvedere: A Fashion District art-deco hotel whose ballroom hosts the charity galas Bruce Wayne arrives late to.
notes.The Excelsior: Old Gotham's grand hotel, chandeliers and a doorman in livery; Gotham's old families have wedded here for a century.
notes.The Regency: The Upper East Side's five-star hotel, presidential suites and a lobby where everybody knows whose money is whose.
notes.Cherry Hills Prep: A private school in Cherry Hills with a lacrosse obsession and a waiting list from birth.
notes.Gotham Heights High: An Upper West Side public high school with a good debate team and a terrible roof.
notes.PS 117: Bristol's public elementary, small and leafy, with Wayne Foundation computers and a gardening club.
notes.Robinson High: Coventry's high school, named for the park, with a football team that hasn't won since 1987.
notes.St. Mary's School: A Kane Heights Catholic school with plaid uniforms and nuns who've seen everything.
notes.Bluebird Boutique: A Diamond District boutique for one-off pieces, where Selina browses and the security guard pretends not to notice.
notes.Ellison's Jewelers: Old Gotham's oldest jeweller, robbed eleven times; the twelfth robber is, by tradition, Catwoman.
notes.Gotham Books: The Fashion District's big bookshop, four floors and a café; Tim's got a tab in true crime.
notes.Hart & Sons Tailors: A Burnside tailor three generations deep; they've let out suits for men with very unusual shoulders and asked nothing.
notes.Madame Lacroix: An Upper East Side couture house where Gotham's society women order gowns a year before the gala.
notes.Rook & Pawn: A Chinatown pawnshop and chess hall; stolen goods move through the back, chess games through the front.
notes.Second Story Books: A Fashion District used bookshop up a narrow staircase, its name a cat burglar's joke the owner swears is innocent.
notes.The Record Room: A Fashion District record shop, crates of vinyl and listening booths; Dick sends Bruce photos of jazz records he'll never play.
notes.Vintage Vault: A Burnside vintage shop in an old bank, clothes racks in the vault and a cash register that was there for the last robbery.
